judgment.zh_hant: 元亨。利涉大川，先甲三日，後甲三日。
judgment.zh_hans: 元亨。利涉大川，先甲三日，后甲三日。
judgment.en_legge: Ku indicates great progress and success (to him who deals properly with the condition represented by it). There will be advantage in (efforts like that of) crossing the great stream. (He should weigh well, however, the events of) three days before the turning point, and those (to be done) three days after it.

tuan.zh_hant: 蠱、剛上而柔下，巽而止，蠱。蠱元亨，而天下治也。利涉大川、往有事也。先甲三日、後甲三日，終則有始，天行也。
tuan.zh_hans: 蛊、刚上而柔下，巽而止，蛊。蛊元亨，而天下治也。利涉大川、往有事也。先甲三日、后甲三日，终则有始，天行也。
tuan.en_legge: In Ku we have the strong (trigram) above, and the weak one below; we have (below) pliancy, and (above) stopping:—these give the idea of Ku (a Troublous Condition of affairs verging to ruin). 'Ku indicates great progress and success:'—(through the course shown in it), all under heaven, there will be good order. 'There will be advantage in crossing the great stream:'—he who advances will encounter the business to be done. '(He should weigh well, however, the events of) three days before (the turning-point), and those (to be done) three days after it:'—the end (of confusion) is the beginning (of order); such is the procedure of Heaven.

image.zh_hant: 山下有風，蠱。君子以振民育德。
image.zh_hans: 山下有风，蛊。君子以振民育德。
image.en_legge: (The trigram for) a mountain, and below it that for wind, form Ku. The superior man, in accordance with this, (addresses himself to) help the people and nourish his own virtue.

text.zh_hant: 幹父之蠱，有子，考无咎，厲終吉。
text.zh_hans: 干父之蛊，有子，考无咎，厉终吉。
text.en_legge: The first line, divided, shows (a son) dealing with the troubles caused by his father. If he be an (able) son, the father will escape the blame of having erred. The position is perilous, but there will be good fortune in the end.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'He deals with the troubles caused by his father:'—he feels that he has entered into the work of his father.

text.en_legge: The second line, undivided, shows (a son) dealing with the troubles caused by his mother. He should not (carry) his firm correctness (to the utmost).

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'He deals with the troubles caused by his mother:'—he holds to the course of the due mean.

text.zh_hant: 幹父之蠱，小有悔，无大咎。
text.zh_hans: 干父之蛊，小有悔，无大咎。
text.en_legge: The third line, undivided, shows (a son) dealing with the troubles caused by his father. There may be some small occasion for repentance, but there will not be any great error.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'He deals with the troubles caused by his father:' in the end there will be no error.

text.en_legge: The fourth line, divided, shows (a son) viewing indulgently the troubles caused by his father. If he go forward, he will find cause to regret it.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'He views indulgently the troubles caused by his father:'—if he go forward, he will not succeed.

text.en_legge: The fifth line, divided, shows (a son) dealing with the troubles caused by his father. He obtains the praise of using (the fit instrument for his work).

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'He deals with the troubles caused by his father, and obtains praise:'—he is responded to (by the subject of line two) with all his virtue.

text.en_legge: The sixth line, undivided, shows us one who does not serve either king or feudal lord, but in a lofty spirit prefers (to attend to) his own affairs.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'He does not serve either king or feudal lord:'-—but his aim may be a model (to others).
